# Pathway Enrichment and Multi-Omics Abundance Profiles

Pathway enrichment and multi-omics profiling aggregate molecular alterations into functional signatures. This chapter covers Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA), multi-omics pathway enrichment across RNA, single-cell transcriptomics, mass spectrometry proteomics, and microbiome metagenomics, bubble heatmap archetypes, and rank-abundance dynamic range curves.

## Gene Set Enrichment Analysis: `type = "gsea"` and `type = "gsea_running"`

Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (Subramanian et al., *PNAS* 2005) evaluates whether an a priori defined gene set $S$ shows cumulative enrichment at the extremes of a ranked gene list $L$:

$$P_{\text{hit}}(S, i) = \sum_{g_j \in S, j \le i} \frac{|r_j|^p}{N_R}, \quad N_R = \sum_{g_j \in S} |r_j|^p$$

$$P_{\text{miss}}(S, i) = \sum_{g_j \notin S, j \le i} \frac{1}{N - N_H}$$

$$ES(S) = \arg\max_{i} |P_{\text{hit}}(S, i) - P_{\text{miss}}(S, i)|$$

`cliomicplot` provides four complementary visualizations for GSEA results:
1. **Preranked Enrichment Dot Plot (`type = "gsea"`)**: Pathway terms ranked by effect magnitude, with dot size encoding $-\log_{10}(\text{FDR})$ and fill encoding Normalized Enrichment Score (NES).
2. **Three-Tier Running Score Walk Plot (`type = "gsea_running"`)**: The classical GSEA profile displaying the cumulative walk curve, gene hit barcode rug, and ranked metric area.
3. **Directional Diverging Lollipop Plot (`type = "lollipop"`)**: Horizontal effect size bars comparing positive and negative pathway activation.
4. **Multi-Phenotype Comparison Matrix (`type = type_bubble_diverging()`)**: Cross-condition pathway activity across disease phenotypes and therapeutic stages.

### Example 1: Preranked Pathway Enrichment Dot Plot (with `fgsea`)

The preranked dot plot displays enriched pathways calculated by `fgsea::fgseaMultilevel()` using differential expression statistics, sorting terms by Normalized Enrichment Score (NES):

```{r gsea-dotplot-demo, fig.width=8.0, fig.height=5.5}
library(cliomicplot)
library(ggplot2)
library(fgsea)

# Step 1: Load DESeq2 differential statistics from bundled GEO dermatology dataset
series <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "geo_dermatology_series_de.rds", package = "cliomicplot"))
de_tbl <- series[["ad_vs_hc"]]

ranks <- de_tbl$stat
names(ranks) <- de_tbl$gene
ranks <- sort(na.omit(ranks), decreasing = TRUE)

# Step 2: Define cutaneous pathways
kegg_skin_pathways <- list(
  "Cytokine-Cytokine Receptor"  = c("IL4R", "IL13RA1", "IL1RL1", "IL33", "TSLP", "CCR7", "CXCL8"),
  "JAK-STAT Signaling Pathway"  = c("STAT6", "STAT3", "JAK1", "JAK2", "SOCS1", "SOCS3"),
  "Chemokine Signaling Pathway" = c("CCL17", "CCL18", "CCL22", "CCL26", "CXCL1", "CXCL2"),
  "Antimicrobial Defense"       = c("DEFB4A", "S100A7", "S100A8", "S100A9", "S100A12", "PI3"),
  "Epidermal Differentiation"   = c("FLG", "LOR", "IVL", "LCE3A", "LCE3D", "LCE3E", "SPRR2G"),
  "Fatty Acid Metabolism"       = c("FASN", "ELOVL3", "ELOVL4", "ELOVL6", "SCD", "ACACA")
)

# Step 3: Run fast preranked GSEA using fgsea package
fgsea_res <- fgsea::fgseaMultilevel(
  pathways = kegg_skin_pathways,
  stats    = ranks,
  minSize  = 3
)

clitheme("nature")

# Step 4: Render publication dot plot via type_gsea()
p_gsea <- cliplot(
  as.data.frame(fgsea_res),
  type     = "gsea",
  top_term = 10,
  title    = "fgsea Normalized Enrichment Scores Across Cutaneous Pathways"
)
p_gsea
```

### Example 2: Three-Tier GSEA Running Enrichment Score Walk

The running enrichment score walk illustrates the cumulative enrichment score $ES(i)$ across ranked genes, identifying the leading-edge subset that accounts for peak enrichment:

```{r gsea-running-demo, fig.width=8.2, fig.height=6.2}
set.seed(42)

# Simulate transcriptome ranking of 1,200 genes sorted by differential expression t-statistic
all_genes <- paste0("Gene_", seq_len(1200))
stats <- sort(rnorm(1200, mean = 0, sd = 2.0), decreasing = TRUE)
names(stats) <- all_genes

# Define target gene set (40 genes enriched at the top of the ranked list)
pathway_hits <- all_genes[c(seq(2, 80, by = 2), seq(90, 300, by = 20))]

# Compute exact running enrichment walk using Subramanian algorithm
walk_df <- cli_calc_gsea_running(stats, pathway_hits, p = 1.0)

# Render 3-tier composite: Running ES curve, Barcode rug, and Ranked metric gradient
p_running <- cliplot(
  walk_df,
  type = type_gsea_running(
    line_col     = "#1B7837",
    line_width   = 1.1,
    barcode_col  = "#182033",
    show_metric  = TRUE,
    peak_color   = "#D73027",
    pathway_name = "Hallmark IL-4 / IL-13 Signaling Pathway",
    nes          = 2.45,
    fdr          = 0.0001
  )
)
p_running
```

### Example 3: Directional Diverging Lollipop Enrichment Plot

Horizontal lollipops provide a clean visualization of pathway activation versus repression relative to the zero null baseline:

```{r gsea-lollipop-demo, fig.width=8.0, fig.height=4.8}
pathway_subset <- c(
  "Cytokine-Cytokine Receptor", "JAK-STAT Cascade", "Th2 Differentiation",
  "Chemokine Cascade", "NF-kB Activation", "IL-17 Signaling",
  "Fatty Acid Metabolism", "Keratinization", "Steroid Biosynthesis"
)
nes_subset <- c(2.65, 2.38, 2.08, 1.95, 1.88, 1.72, -1.65, -1.98, -2.45)

lollipop_df <- data.frame(
  Term = pathway_subset,
  NES  = nes_subset,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
lollipop_df$Term <- factor(lollipop_df$Term, levels = lollipop_df$Term[order(lollipop_df$NES)])

clitheme("science")

p_lollipop <- cliplot(
  NES ~ Term,
  data = lollipop_df,
  type = type_lollipop(
    point_size  = 3.8,
    stem_width  = 0.8,
    point_color = "#3B4992"
  ),
  title = "Directional Pathway Enrichment Relative to Zero Baseline",
  xlab  = "Normalized Enrichment Score (NES)"
) +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50", linewidth = 0.4)
p_lollipop
```

### Example 4: Multi-Phenotype GSEA Comparison Matrix

Comparing pathway enrichment across multiple experimental contrasts reveals shared inflammatory mechanisms and disease-specific divergences:

```{r gsea-comparison-matrix-demo, fig.width=8.5, fig.height=5.8}
set.seed(101)
pheno_pathways <- c(
  "IL-4 / IL-13 Signaling", "Th2 Differentiation", "JAK-STAT Cascade",
  "Chemokine Receptor Activity", "Epidermal Differentiation", "Lipid Synthesis"
)
comparisons <- c("AD LS vs Healthy", "AD NL vs Healthy", "AD LS vs NL", "Dupilumab W16")

multi_gsea <- expand.grid(Pathway = pheno_pathways, Comparison = comparisons, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
multi_gsea$NES <- c(
  2.6, 0.8, 2.1, -1.8,
  2.3, 0.5, 1.9, -1.6,
  1.9, 0.6, 1.5, -1.2,
  2.0, 0.4, 1.7, -1.1,
  -2.4, -0.6, -2.1, 1.8,
  -2.1, -0.4, -1.8, 1.5
)
multi_gsea$FDR <- c(
  1e-4, 0.08, 2e-4, 5e-4,
  3e-4, 0.12, 4e-4, 8e-4,
  2e-3, 0.10, 5e-3, 0.01,
  1e-3, 0.15, 3e-3, 0.02,
  2e-4, 0.09, 3e-4, 1e-3,
  5e-4, 0.14, 8e-4, 2e-3
)

clitheme("nature")

p_multi_gsea <- cliplot(
  Pathway ~ Comparison,
  data       = multi_gsea,
  by         = -log10(multi_gsea$FDR),
  type       = type_bubble_diverging(
    palette      = "nature",
    midpoint     = 0,
    max_size     = 7.5,
    stroke_col   = "grey30",
    stroke_width = 0.35,
    size_name    = expression(-log[10]~italic(q)),
    fill_name    = "NES"
  ),
  extra_data = list(fill = multi_gsea$NES),
  title      = "Cross-Phenotype Pathway Enrichment Concordance",
  subtitle   = "Circle size encodes -log10 q; fill encodes Normalized Enrichment Score (NES)"
)
p_multi_gsea
```

## Multi-Omics Pathway Enrichment Directly from Biomarker Lists

Clinical and translational investigations frequently yield candidate biomarker lists without full raw count matrices. This section demonstrates how to run functional pathway enrichment using standard Bioconductor packages (`clusterProfiler`, `org.Hs.eg.db`) starting directly from bare lists of biomarker symbols across four omics layers:
- **Bulk RNA Biomarker List**: Query GO Biological Process pathways from a character vector of gene symbols via `clusterProfiler::enrichGO()`.
- **Single-cell Lineage Biomarker Lists**: Compare cell-type-specific biomarker sets in one call using `clusterProfiler::compareCluster()`.
- **Proteomics Biomarker List**: Map protein biomarker hits to subcellular complexes (cornified envelope, desmosomes) via `clusterProfiler::enrichGO(ont = "CC")`.
- **Microbial Functional Biomarkers**: Test candidate dysbiosis biomarker pathways across anatomical microenvironments.

### Bulk RNA Gene Biomarker List: Pathway Enrichment with `clusterProfiler`

When biomarker discovery identifies a candidate gene panel, `clusterProfiler::enrichGO()` tests for over-representation against the human genome annotation (`org.Hs.eg.db`):

```{r multiomics-rna-ora-atoz, fig.width=8.5, fig.height=5.6}
library(clusterProfiler)
library(org.Hs.eg.db)
library(ggplot2)

# Step 1: Input list of candidate gene biomarkers
rna_biomarkers <- c(
  "CCL17", "CCL18", "CCL22", "IL4R", "IL13RA1", "STAT6", "POSTN",
  "S100A7", "S100A8", "S100A9", "DEFB4A", "PI3",
  "FLG", "LOR", "IVL", "LCE3A", "SPRR2G",
  "SERPINB3", "SERPINB4", "SPINK5"
)

# Step 2: Run GO Biological Process enrichment directly from biomarker symbols
ego_bp <- clusterProfiler::enrichGO(
  gene          = rna_biomarkers,
  OrgDb         = org.Hs.eg.db,
  keyType       = "SYMBOL",
  ont           = "BP",
  pAdjustMethod = "BH",
  pvalueCutoff  = 0.05,
  qvalueCutoff  = 0.05
)

# Step 3: Extract results and compute numeric Gene Ratio
ego_df <- as.data.frame(ego_bp)
ego_df$NumericGeneRatio <- vapply(
  strsplit(ego_df$GeneRatio, "/"),
  function(x) as.numeric(x[1]) / as.numeric(x[2]),
  numeric(1)
)

top_go <- head(ego_df, 8)
top_go$Description <- factor(top_go$Description, levels = rev(top_go$Description))

# Step 4: Render publication dot plot
clitheme("nature")

p_rna_ora <- ggplot2::ggplot(top_go, ggplot2::aes(x = NumericGeneRatio, y = Description)) +
  ggplot2::geom_segment(
    ggplot2::aes(x = 0, xend = NumericGeneRatio, y = Description, yend = Description),
    color = "grey75", linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    ggplot2::aes(size = Count, fill = -log10(p.adjust)),
    shape = 21, color = "grey25", stroke = 0.45
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_gradientn(
    colours = c("#EFF3FF", "#6BAED6", "#2171B5", "#08519C"),
    name = expression(-log[10]~italic(q))
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_size_area(max_size = 7.5, name = "Biomarker Hits") +
  theme_cli_nature() +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Gene Ratio (k / |Biomarkers|)",
    y = NULL,
    title = "GO Biological Process Enrichment from Biomarker List",
    subtitle = "Calculated via clusterProfiler::enrichGO() using human genome background"
  )
p_rna_ora
```

Antimicrobial humoral response was the top enriched biological process ($q = 8.66 \times 10^{-10}$, 8 hits), followed by epidermal cell differentiation ($q = 1.74 \times 10^{-8}$, 7 hits) and keratinocyte differentiation ($q = 1.42 \times 10^{-7}$, 6 hits).

### Single-Cell Lineage Biomarker Lists: Cross-Cluster Enrichment with `compareCluster`

Single-cell marker discovery produces distinct biomarker lists for each cell cluster. `clusterProfiler::compareCluster()` evaluates all lineage biomarker lists simultaneously:

```{r multiomics-scrna-pathway-atoz, fig.width=8.5, fig.height=5.8}
# Step 1: Input named lists of lineage-specific biomarkers
sc_biomarker_lists <- list(
  "Th2 / ILC2"       = c("IL4R", "IL13RA1", "STAT6", "CCL17", "CCL22", "GATA3"),
  "Suprabasal KC"    = c("FLG", "LOR", "IVL", "LCE3A", "SPRR2G", "KRT1", "KRT10"),
  "Inflammatory KC"  = c("S100A7", "S100A8", "S100A9", "DEFB4A", "PI3"),
  "cDC2 / Myeloid"   = c("HLA-DRA", "HLA-DRB1", "CD74", "CD86", "FCER1A")
)

# Step 2: Compare enrichment across all lineages simultaneously
comp_res <- clusterProfiler::compareCluster(
  geneCluster   = sc_biomarker_lists,
  fun           = "enrichGO",
  OrgDb         = org.Hs.eg.db,
  keyType       = "SYMBOL",
  ont           = "BP",
  pAdjustMethod = "BH",
  pvalueCutoff  = 0.05
)

comp_df <- as.data.frame(comp_res)

# Select top 2 terms per lineage cluster
top_comp <- do.call(rbind, lapply(unique(comp_df$Cluster), function(cl) {
  head(comp_df[comp_df$Cluster == cl, ], 2)
}))
top_comp$Description <- factor(top_comp$Description, levels = rev(unique(top_comp$Description)))

# Step 3: Render cross-lineage bubble heatmap
clitheme("cell")

p_sc_path <- cliplot(
  Description ~ Cluster,
  data = top_comp,
  by   = top_comp$Count,
  type = type_bubble_circle(
    palette      = "plasma",
    max_size     = 7.5,
    stroke_col   = "grey35",
    stroke_width = 0.35,
    size_name    = "Hit Count",
    fill_name    = expression(-log[10]~italic(q))
  ),
  extra_data = list(fill = -log10(top_comp$p.adjust)),
  title      = "Lineage-Resolved Biomarker Enrichment via compareCluster",
  subtitle   = "Point size reflects biomarker hit count; colour reflects -log10 q"
)
p_sc_path
```

Th2/ILC2 biomarkers enriched for response to interleukin-4 ($q = 8.14 \times 10^{-9}$, 4 hits), while suprabasal keratinocyte markers enriched for epidermal differentiation ($q = 2.15 \times 10^{-8}$, 6 hits).

### Mass Spectrometry Proteomics Biomarker List: GO Cellular Component Enrichment

Quantitative proteomics screens identify differentially abundant protein panels. `clusterProfiler::enrichGO(ont = "CC")` maps protein biomarkers directly to subcellular macromolecular complexes:

```{r multiomics-proteomics-modules-atoz, fig.width=8.5, fig.height=5.8}
# Step 1: Input list of verified protein biomarkers
prot_biomarkers <- c(
  "FLG", "LOR", "IVL", "LCE3D", "SPRR2A",
  "DSC1", "DSG1", "DSP", "PKP1",
  "SPINK5", "SERPINB3", "SERPINB4",
  "S100A7", "S100A8", "DEFB4A"
)

# Step 2: Query GO Cellular Component (subcellular complexes)
ego_cc <- clusterProfiler::enrichGO(
  gene          = prot_biomarkers,
  OrgDb         = org.Hs.eg.db,
  keyType       = "SYMBOL",
  ont           = "CC",
  pAdjustMethod = "BH",
  pvalueCutoff  = 0.05
)

cc_df <- head(as.data.frame(ego_cc), 6)
cc_df$NumericGeneRatio <- vapply(
  strsplit(cc_df$GeneRatio, "/"),
  function(x) as.numeric(x[1]) / as.numeric(x[2]),
  numeric(1)
)
cc_df$Description <- factor(cc_df$Description, levels = rev(cc_df$Description))

# Step 3: Render publication diamond dot plot
clitheme("nature")

p_prot_mod <- ggplot2::ggplot(cc_df, ggplot2::aes(x = NumericGeneRatio, y = Description)) +
  ggplot2::geom_segment(
    ggplot2::aes(x = 0, xend = NumericGeneRatio, y = Description, yend = Description),
    color = "grey75", linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    ggplot2::aes(size = Count, fill = -log10(p.adjust)),
    shape = 23, color = "grey25", stroke = 0.5
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_gradientn(
    colours = c("#FFF5EB", "#FDAE6B", "#E6550D", "#7F2704"),
    name = expression(-log[10]~italic(q))
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_size_area(max_size = 8.0, name = "Protein Hits") +
  theme_cli_nature() +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Gene Ratio (k / |Biomarkers|)",
    y = NULL,
    title = "Proteomics Biomarker Cellular Component Enrichment",
    subtitle = "Tested via clusterProfiler::enrichGO(ont = 'CC') mapping to macromolecular complexes"
  )
p_prot_mod
```

Cornified envelope had the highest significance among cellular components ($q = 1.12 \times 10^{-7}$, 5 hits), followed by desmosome assembly complexes ($q = 3.45 \times 10^{-6}$, 4 hits).

### Cutaneous Microbiome Functional Metagenomics (MetaCyc Pathways): A to Z Pipeline

Shotgun metagenomics profiles metabolic pathway abundance across skin microenvironments. The pipeline:

1. Filters low-prevalence pathways (detected in $< 20\%$ of samples).
2. Stabilizes variance with $\log_2(\text{CPM} + 1)$ transformation.
3. Tests differential abundance between flare and remission with Wilcoxon rank-sum tests.
4. Corrects for multiple testing across pathways and anatomical microenvironments.

```{r multiomics-microbiome-metacyc-atoz, fig.width=8.5, fig.height=5.8}
# Step 1: Input MetaCyc functional pathway counts (CPM) across skin sites
set.seed(42)
metacyc_paths <- c(
  "Staphyloferrin Siderophore Biosynthesis",
  "Peptidoglycan Maturation",
  "Lipoteichoic Acid Biosynthesis",
  "SCFA (Butyrate) Production",
  "L-Arginine Degradation",
  "Bile Acid Hydrolysis"
)
sites <- c("Antecubital Fossa", "Volar Forearm", "Forehead")
n_subj <- 12

# Step 2 & 3: Differential testing (Flare vs Remission) per site
mb_results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(sites, function(st) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(metacyc_paths, function(pwy) {
    flare_mean <- if (grepl("Staphyloferrin|Peptidoglycan|Lipoteichoic", pwy)) 5.2 else 2.1
    remis_mean <- if (grepl("Staphyloferrin|Peptidoglycan|Lipoteichoic", pwy)) 2.3 else 4.5
    
    flare_cpm <- pmax(0, rnorm(n_subj, mean = flare_mean, sd = 0.7))
    remis_cpm <- pmax(0, rnorm(n_subj, mean = remis_mean, sd = 0.7))
    
    wt <- wilcox.test(flare_cpm, remis_cpm)
    log2fc <- mean(flare_cpm) - mean(remis_cpm)
    prev <- mean(c(flare_cpm, remis_cpm) > 0.5) * 100
    
    data.frame(
      Pathway    = pwy,
      Site       = st,
      Log2FC     = log2fc,
      Prevalence = prev,
      pvalue     = wt$p.value,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }))
}))

# Step 4: Adjust p-values across all tests
mb_results$padj    <- p.adjust(mb_results$pvalue, method = "BH")
mb_results$negLogQ <- -log10(mb_results$padj)

# Step 5: Render diverging bubble heatmap across anatomical microenvironments
clitheme("nature")

p_mb_metacyc <- cliplot(
  Pathway ~ Site,
  data       = mb_results,
  by         = mb_results$negLogQ,
  type       = type_bubble_diverging(
    palette      = "rdbu",
    midpoint     = 0,
    max_size     = 8.0,
    stroke_col   = "grey35",
    stroke_width = 0.35,
    size_name    = expression(-log[10]~italic(q)),
    fill_name    = expression(log[2]~"FC (Flare / Remission)")
  ),
  extra_data = list(fill = mb_results$Log2FC),
  title      = "Cutaneous Microbiome Functional Metagenomics (MetaCyc Pathways)",
  subtitle   = "Circle size encodes -log10 q; fill encodes flare vs remission log2(FC)"
)
p_mb_metacyc
```

Staphyloferrin siderophore biosynthesis had elevated abundance in flare lesions across all three cutaneous sites (antecubital fossa $\log_2(\text{FC}) = 3.79$, $q = 9.51 \times 10^{-7}$), whereas short-chain fatty acid production decreased ($\log_2(\text{FC}) = -2.46$, $q = 9.51 \times 10^{-7}$).


## Bubble Heatmap Archetypes: `type = "bubble_heatmap"`

Bubble heatmaps display two continuous variables across features (rows) and conditions (columns). Point size encodes magnitude, count, or significance; fill colour encodes directional effect size ($\log_2\text{FC}$, NES) or continuous significance ($-\log_{10}P$).

`cliomicplot` provides five bubble forms:
1. **Diamond Bubble Matrix**: classic diamond glyphs with alternating row bands.
2. **Circular Dot Bubble Matrix with Divergent Palette**: circular dots centered on zero to show positive and negative regulation.
3. **Significance-Glyph Annotated Matrix**: bubbles with significance asterisks (`*`, `**`, `***`) based on adjusted $P$-values.
4. **Square / Tile-Scaled Matrix**: proportional square glyphs in a tile grid.
5. **Directional Triangle Bubble Matrix**: oriented triangles indicating directional modulation across experimental cohorts.

### Form 1: Classic Diamond Bubble Matrix

Diamond bubble matrices display effect magnitude as diamond area and statistical significance as fill colour. Values exceeding `label_threshold` are labelled directly inside the glyphs.

```{r bubble-diamond-demo, fig.width=8.5, fig.height=6.2}
set.seed(42)
proteins <- c("APOE", "MAPT", "APP", "SNCA", "GFAP", "NEFL", "VIM", "SYN1", "GAP43", "UCHL1")
contrasts <- c("AD vs Control", "PD vs Control", "AD vs PD", "Severe vs Mild")

bh_df <- expand.grid(Protein = proteins, Comparison = contrasts, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
bh_df$absFC <- runif(nrow(bh_df), 0.2, 3.5)
bh_df$negLogP <- runif(nrow(bh_df), 1.0, 15.0)

clitheme("cell")

p_diamond <- cliplot(
  Protein ~ Comparison,
  data       = bh_df,
  by         = bh_df$absFC,
  type       = type_bubble_diamond(
    max_size        = 8.0,
    size_name       = "|log2FC|",
    fill_name       = expression(-log[10]~P),
    fill_low        = "#4575B4",
    fill_mid        = "#FFFFBF",
    fill_high       = "#D73027"
  ),
  extra_data = list(fill = bh_df$negLogP),
  title      = "Diamond Bubble Matrix: Neurodegenerative Biomarkers",
  subtitle   = "Point size reflects |log2FC|; colour gradient reflects -log10 P"
)
p_diamond
```

### Form 2: Circular Dot Bubble Matrix with Divergent Palette

For bidirectional metrics such as Normalized Enrichment Scores (NES) or signed $\log_2\text{FC}$, `type_bubble_diverging()` applies a diverging colour gradient centered at 0 (e.g. `palette = "nature"`: navy to white to red). Bubble radius represents $-\log_{10}q$.

```{r bubble-circle-diverging-demo, fig.width=8.5, fig.height=6.2}
set.seed(101)
pathways_circ <- c(
  "IL-4 / IL-13 Signaling", "Th2 Differentiation", "JAK-STAT Cascade",
  "NF-kB Activation", "Epidermal Barrier", "Keratinization",
  "Lipid Metabolism", "Interferon Gamma Response"
)
stages <- c("Acute Lesional", "Chronic Lesional", "Non-Lesional", "Dupilumab W16")

da_df <- expand.grid(Pathway = pathways_circ, Stage = stages, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
da_df$NES <- c(
  2.4, 2.8, 0.4, -1.8,
  2.1, 2.5, 0.2, -1.5,
  1.8, 2.2, 0.5, -1.2,
  1.9, 1.7, 0.3, -0.9,
  -2.2, -2.6, -0.3, 1.9,
  -2.5, -3.1, -0.5, 2.2,
  -1.7, -2.1, -0.2, 1.4,
  0.6, 1.2, 0.1, -0.4
)
da_df$negLogQ <- runif(nrow(da_df), 1.5, 12.0)

clitheme("nature")

p_circ <- cliplot(
  Pathway ~ Stage,
  data       = da_df,
  by         = da_df$negLogQ,
  type       = type_bubble_diverging(
    palette      = "nature",
    midpoint     = 0,
    max_size     = 7.5,
    stroke_col   = "grey30",
    stroke_width = 0.35,
    size_name    = expression(-log[10]~italic(q)),
    fill_name    = "NES"
  ),
  extra_data = list(fill = da_df$NES),
  title      = "Inflammatory Pathway Modulation Across Disease Stages",
  subtitle   = "Circle size encodes -log10 q; diverging fill encodes Normalized Enrichment Score"
)
p_circ
```

### Form 3: Significance-Glyph Overlaid Matrix

When statistical significance requires explicit discrete thresholds ($* p < 0.05$, $** p < 0.01$, $*** p < 0.001$), `label_metric = "signif"` prints asterisks directly onto the bubbles.

```{r bubble-signif-demo, fig.width=8.5, fig.height=6.2}
set.seed(202)
cytokines <- c("IL4", "IL13", "IL22", "IL31", "CCL17", "CCL18", "CCL26", "CXCL10", "IFNG", "IL1B")
timepoints <- c("Baseline", "Week 4", "Week 16", "Week 52")

cyt_df <- expand.grid(Cytokine = cytokines, Timepoint = timepoints, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
cyt_df$log2FC <- runif(nrow(cyt_df), 0.2, 4.0)
cyt_df$negLogP <- runif(nrow(cyt_df), 0.5, 8.0)

clitheme("science")

p_signif <- cliplot(
  Cytokine ~ Timepoint,
  data       = cyt_df,
  by         = cyt_df$log2FC,
  type       = type_bubble_heatmap(
    shape          = "circle",
    palette        = "viridis",
    label_metric   = "signif",
    signif_cutoffs = c(0.05, 0.01, 0.001),
    label_size     = 3.2,
    label_col      = "white",
    stroke_col     = "grey35",
    stroke_width   = 0.4,
    size_name      = expression(log[2]~"FC"),
    fill_name      = expression(-log[10]~P)
  ),
  extra_data = list(fill = cyt_df$negLogP),
  title      = "Cutaneous Biomarker Response Kinetics",
  subtitle   = "Asterisks denote significance tiers (* p < 0.05, ** p < 0.01, *** p < 0.001)"
)
p_signif
```

### Form 4: Square / Tile-Scaled Matrix

Proportional squares in a tile grid display cell density, taxon abundance, or cross-cohort concordance.

```{r bubble-square-demo, fig.width=8.5, fig.height=6.0}
set.seed(303)
taxa <- c("S. aureus", "S. epidermidis", "C. acnes", "M. restricta", "P. melaninogenica", "C. striatum")
sites <- c("Volar Forearm", "Antecubital Fossa", "Forehead", "Cheek", "Retroauricular")

taxa_df <- expand.grid(Taxon = taxa, Site = sites, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
taxa_df$Abundance <- runif(nrow(taxa_df), 1.0, 30.0)
taxa_df$Prevalence <- runif(nrow(taxa_df), 20.0, 95.0)

clitheme("nejm")

p_square <- cliplot(
  Taxon ~ Site,
  data       = taxa_df,
  by         = taxa_df$Abundance,
  type       = type_bubble_square(
    palette      = "mako",
    max_size     = 8.0,
    stroke_col   = "white",
    stroke_width = 0.5,
    size_name    = "Rel. Abund (%)",
    fill_name    = "Prevalence (%)"
  ),
  extra_data = list(fill = taxa_df$Prevalence),
  title      = "Microbial Colonization Density Across Skin Microenvironments",
  subtitle   = "Square area reflects relative abundance; fill intensity reflects cohort prevalence"
)
p_square
```

### Form 5: Directional Triangle Bubble Matrix

Directional triangles (`shape = "triangle_up"` or `"triangle_down"`) emphasize activation or repression across experimental screens.

```{r bubble-triangle-demo, fig.width=8.5, fig.height=6.0}
set.seed(404)
genes <- c("STAT3", "STAT6", "GATA3", "TBX21", "RORC", "FOXP3", "NFKB1", "RELA")
treatments <- c("Vehicle", "IL-4 Stim", "JAKi (Baricitinib)", "Biologic (Dupilumab)")

tri_df <- expand.grid(Gene = genes, Treatment = treatments, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
tri_df$Score <- runif(nrow(tri_df), 0.5, 5.0)
tri_df$Activity <- runif(nrow(tri_df), 1.0, 10.0)

clitheme("nature")

p_tri <- cliplot(
  Gene ~ Treatment,
  data       = tri_df,
  by         = tri_df$Score,
  type       = type_bubble_heatmap(
    shape        = "triangle_up",
    palette      = "rocket",
    grid_style   = "banded",
    max_size     = 8.0,
    stroke_col   = "white",
    stroke_width = 0.6,
    size_name    = "TF Score",
    fill_name    = "Activity Index"
  ),
  extra_data = list(fill = tri_df$Activity),
  title      = "Transcription Factor Activity Profile",
  subtitle   = "Triangle area encodes binding score; fill denotes computed activity index"
)
p_tri
```

## Rank-Abundance Dynamic Range Curves: `type = "rankabundance"`

In quantitative proteomics, rank-abundance curves visualize the dynamic range of protein detection across orders of magnitude:

```{r rank-abundance-demo, fig.width=8.0, fig.height=5.0}
set.seed(42)
n_prot <- 800
intensities <- sort(10^rnorm(n_prot, mean = 6.5, sd = 1.1), decreasing = TRUE)
ranks <- seq_len(n_prot)

rank_df <- data.frame(
  Rank      = ranks,
  Intensity = intensities,
  Protein   = paste0("Prot_", ranks)
)

clitheme("science")

p_rank <- cliplot(
  Intensity ~ Rank,
  data = rank_df,
  type = type_rankabundance(
    log_scale     = "10",
    point_color   = "#4DBBD5",
    marginal_type = "density",
    label_genes   = c("Prot_1", "Prot_10", "Prot_50", "Prot_200"),
    label_color   = "#E64B35",
    label_size    = 3.0
  ),
  title    = "Dynamic Range of Proteome Detection",
  subtitle = "Protein abundance spanning ~5 orders of magnitude with marginal density",
  xlab     = "Abundance Rank",
  ylab     = "LFQ Intensity"
)
p_rank
```
